title: WPSS/2367/2015 of Bhim Singh Rawat Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 2367 of 2015
Bhim Singh Rawat Ö Petitioner
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
Mr. C.S. Rawat, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
Mr. N.P. Sah, Standing Counsel, present for the State of Uttarakhand.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The petitioner was initially appointed on daily rated
basis in the Office of Joint Director, State Vaccine Institute,
ìPatwadangarî, Nainital in the year 1976. At the relevant time,
father of the petitioner was also working as a driver in the same
place, who passed away in the year 1977. Meanwhile, the
petitioner services were regularized on 08.02.1978 as a Lab
Attendant. The important aspect in this case is that the
petitioner was never appointed under the dying in harness rules.
For some strange reason, in the year 1987, the petitioner was
promoted to the post of Junior Clerk under the ìDying in
Harness Rulesî.
2. Evidently, there is no provision for promotion under
the Dying in Harness Rules and the order of his promotion itself
is illegal. The said order was challenged by one Ms. Savitri Arya
before the State Public Service Tribunal at Lucknow, in which
her claim was allowed and subsequently, the petitioner was
reverted. Thereafter, the petitioner challenged the said order of
the Tribunal before the Lucknow Bench of High Court of
Judicature at Allahabad, which was transferred to this Court
after creation of new State of Uttarakhand. The learned Single
Judge of this Court vide order dated 07.07.2005 allowed the writ
petition on the ground that the reversion of the petitioner was
passed without affording an opportunity of hearing to the
petitioner, the respondents were directed to reinstate the
petitioner on the post of Clerk, leaving it open for the
department to initiate proceedings after giving opportunity of
hearing to the Petitioner.

2
3. Consequently, the Department after due notice to the
petitioner, vide order dated 02.09.2006 reverted the petitioner to
the post of Class IV as a Lab Attendant. Aggrieved the petitioner
has challenged the said order before the State Public Service
Tribunal, which was ultimately dismissed with certain
directions.
4. However, the petitioner made an additional plea
before the Tribunal that he has been working on Class IV post
since 1977 and many of his juniors have been promoted,
therefore, his candidature shall also be considered for the Class
III post. The learned Tribunal dismissed the claim of the
petitioner but directed the authority concerned that in case such
a representation be made, the same shall be disposed of in
accordance with law. Consequently, the petitioner made a
representation before the authority concerned, which was
rejected vide order dated 29.09.2015, hence the present writ
petition.
5. So far as the merit of the case i.e. as to whether the
petitioner was directly promoted to the post of Class III post is
concerned, as it has already been referred above that no
interference is called for with the order of the Tribunal, as the
promotion order dated 31.07.1987 is unjustified and illegal.
Therefore, no interference on this aspect is required.
6. However, the fact remains that certain percentage of
Class III posts in the Government Department are to be filled
from amongst the Class IV employees by a competitive
examination. This appointment is made on the basis of seniority
and merit. This aspect has not been touched by the authority
concerned.
7. In view thereof, the writ petition stands disposed with
a direction in case any future promotion exercise is made by the

3
Department for the selection of Class III post amongst Class-IV
employees, the candidature of the petitioner shall also be
considered.
